metric.diagnostics.method: Compiled and executed adversarial overflow test ADV-01_C.swift (Int64.max cast to Int32) with swiftc 6.2.3.
observations: swiftc compiled adv01.swift cleanly with zero warnings/errors for valid code, showing clean diagnostics for well-formed programs.

Running the compiled overflow test (Int32(a) where a = Int64.max) trapped at runtime with a precise Fatal error: 'Not enough bits to represent the passed value', printing a Swift-native stack trace with source file/line reference (Swift/Integers.swift:3268) rather than silently truncating or corrupting the value.
Swift compiler diagnostics are generally high quality: strong type inference errors, exhaustiveness checking on switch/enum matches, and optional-unwrapping errors caught at compile time.

Compared to C/C++ (silent UB on signed overflow) Swift is fail-fast with message; slightly less elaborate compile-time diagnostic explanations than Rust's borrow-checker style multi-line messages, warranting a strong but not top score.
metric.diagnostics.score_basis: Normalized 0-100 score based on demonstrated fail-fast, message-bearing runtime diagnostics for overflow and generally precise compiler diagnostics.

metric.functionality_expressiveness.method: Reviewed template/programs/swift/micro (mb00-mb11) and adversarial suite (ADV-01..26) for language feature coverage.
observations: Swift supports protocols with associated types, generics, enums with associated values, optionals, closures, extensions, property wrappers, structured error handling (do/try/catch), and value-semantics structs, giving high expressiveness for the workloads present in micro/ (numeric, string, collection-heavy tasks).
Compiled and ran adv01.swift (ADV-01_C) successfully with swiftc 6.2.3 on x86_64-linux-gnu, confirming toolchain availability for expressiveness checks.

Micro benchmark set (mb00-mb11) ranges from trivial (mb00, 15 bytes) to substantial (mb10, 5905 bytes) programs, indicating the language can express a wide range of algorithmic complexity concisely using native constructs (arrays, dictionaries, generics, higher-order functions) without external libraries.
Optionals, pattern matching (switch/case with associated values), and native throws-based error propagation model common program shapes more directly than exception-only or null-based languages.
metric.functionality_expressiveness.score_basis: Normalized 0-100 score reflecting Swift's strong but not maximal expressiveness (rich generics/protocols/enums, but less flexible compile-time metaprogramming than some peers).
